sections.title: باب 5 — متن (208)

paras.text: … all citizens should be provided justice without prejudice and narrow-mindedness; non-Muslim citizens should have all social rights, and they should be able to worship in their places of worship freely according to their own religion, creed and sect. Besides this, their aim was that such a state be established where all citizens have the basic facilities of life available, among which food, clothing, housing, health and education facilities are included.
paras.urdu: تعصب اور تنگ نظری کے بغیر تمام شہریوں کو انصاف فراہم ہو، غیر مسلم شہریوں کو تمام سماجی حقوق حاصل ہوں اور وہ اپنے مذہب، عقیدے اور مسلک کے مطابق آزادی سے اپنی عبادت گاہوں میں عبادت کر سکیں۔ اس کے علاوہ ان کا مطمحِ نظر یہی تھا کہ ایک ایسی ریاست قائم ہو جائے جہاں تمام شہریوں کو زندگی کی بنیادی سہولتیں دستیاب ہوں۔ ان میں خوراک، لباس، مکان، صحت اور تعلیم کی سہولتیں شامل ہیں۔
paras.pashto: … ټولو اتباعو ته بې له تعصب او تنګ‌نظرۍ انصاف برابر شي، نامسلمانو اتباعو ته ټول ټولنیز حقونه حاصل وي، او هغوی د خپل مذهب، عقیدې او مسلک سره سم په خپلو عبادت‌ځایونو کې په ازادۍ عبادت وکړای شي. سربېره پر دې د هغه نظر همدا و چې داسې دولت جوړ شي چې ټولو اتباعو ته د ژوند بنسټیزې اسانتیاوې برابرې وي؛ په دې کې د خوړو، جامو، کور، روغتیا او زده‌کړې اسانتیاوې شاملې دي.

paras.text: The purposes and goals of the establishment of Pakistan are different from those countries which came into existence by virtue of some historical, geographical or social accident. The Quaid-e-Azam mentioned the purposes of the establishment of Pakistan in the following way:
paras.urdu: پاکستان کے قیام کے مقاصد اور اہداف ان ممالک سے مختلف ہیں جو کسی تاریخی یا جغرافیائی یا سماجی حادثے کی بدولت معرضِ وجود میں آتے ہیں۔ قائدِ اعظم نے قیامِ پاکستان کے مقاصد کا ذکر درج ذیل طریقے سے کیا تھا؛
paras.pashto: د پاکستان د جوړولو موخې او اهداف له هغو هېوادونو توپیر لري چې د کومې تاریخي، جغرافیايي یا ټولنیزې پېښې په برکت رامنځته کېږي. قاید اعظم د پاکستان د جوړولو موخې په لاندې ډول یادې کړې وې:

paras.text: "There is no doubt in this, that we have attained Pakistan, but this is not the end of our struggle; rather it is the beginning of a journey towards a new purpose. Our responsibilities have increased greatly. In the same proportion there should be an increase in our efforts and resolves too, to fulfil them. Our purpose should not be only this, that we fulfil everyone's need and remove fear; rather we should also respect those values of freedom, brotherhood and equality which Islam has made obligatory upon us."
paras.urdu: ”اس میں کوئی شک نہیں کہ ہم پاکستان حاصل کر چکے ہیں لیکن یہ ہماری جدوجہد کا اختتام نہیں ہے بلکہ ایک نئے مقصد کی طرف سفر کا آغاز ہے۔ ہماری ذمہ داریاں بہت بڑھ گئی ہیں۔ ان کو پورا کرنے کے لیے ہماری کوششوں اور عزائم میں بھی اسی تناسب سے اضافہ ہونا چاہیے۔ ہمارا مقصد صرف یہی نہیں ہونا چاہیے کہ ہم ہر کسی کی ضرورت پوری کریں اور خوف دور کریں بلکہ ہمیں آزادی، اخوت اور مساوات کی ان اقدار کی بھی پاسداری کرنی چاہیے جن کو اسلام نے ہم پر لازم قرار دیا ہے۔“
paras.pashto: «په دې کې هېڅ شک نشته چې موږ پاکستان ترلاسه کړی، خو دا زموږ د هڅې پای نه دی، بلکې د یوې نوې موخې په لور د سفر پیل دی. زموږ مسؤلیتونه ډېر زیات شوي. د هغو د پوره کولو لپاره باید زموږ په هڅو او ارادو کې هم په همدې تناسب زیاتوالی راشي. زموږ موخه باید یوازې دا نه وي چې د هر چا اړتیا پوره کړو او وېره لرې کړو، بلکې د ازادۍ، ورورولۍ او برابرۍ د هغو ارزښتونو درناوی هم وکړو چې اسلام پر موږ لازم ګرځولي.»

paras.text: In the light of the sayings of the Quaid-e-Azam, afterwards the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan passed the Objectives Resolution (Resolution Objectives). In the Objectives Resolution the resolve was expressed that the realm of Pakistan, following Islamic principles like democracy, freedom, tolerance, social justice and brotherhood, will provide all non-Muslim Pakistanis all basic rights. Non-Muslims will have this right, that they can protect their religion and pass life according to their own culture. The law and justice will be supreme, and the judiciary will be made empowered and free for the protection of the basic rights of citizens.

sections.content:
… all citizens should be provided justice without prejudice and narrow-mindedness; non-Muslim citizens should have all social rights, and they should be able to worship in their places of worship freely according to their own religion, creed and sect. Besides this, their aim was that such a state be established where all citizens have the basic facilities of life available, among which food, clothing, housing, health and education facilities are included.

The purposes and goals of the establishment of Pakistan are different from those countries which came into existence by virtue of some historical, geographical or social accident. The Quaid-e-Azam mentioned the purposes of the establishment of Pakistan in the following way:

"There is no doubt in this, that we have attained Pakistan, but this is not the end of our struggle; rather it is the beginning of a journey towards a new purpose. Our responsibilities have increased greatly. In the same proportion there should be an increase in our efforts and resolves too, to fulfil them. Our purpose should not be only this, that we fulfil everyone's need and remove fear; rather we should also respect those values of freedom, brotherhood and equality which Islam has made obligatory upon us."

In the light of the sayings of the Quaid-e-Azam, afterwards the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan passed the Objectives Resolution (Resolution Objectives). In the Objectives Resolution the resolve was expressed that the realm of Pakistan, following Islamic principles like democracy, freedom, tolerance, social justice and brotherhood, will provide all non-Muslim Pakistanis all basic rights. Non-Muslims will have this right, that they can protect their religion and pass life according to their own culture. The law and justice will be supreme, and the judiciary will be made empowered and free for the protection of the basic rights of citizens.

On 11 October 1947, presiding over a session, the thoughts which the Quaid-e-Azam expressed also make it entirely evident how clear and comprehensive the concept of the Islamic welfare realm was in his mind. He (may Allah have mercy on him) had said:

"For the attainment of Pakistan we had been struggling for the last ten years. By the grace of Allah, today it has become a reality. For us the establishment of an autonomous state was not by itself a purpose, but rather a means for the attainment of a higher purpose. We wanted to make such a state in which we could breathe like free people, could pass life according to our Islamic cultural traditions, and golden Islamic principles …

Pakistan determined the following national purposes for the attainment of the Islamic welfare realm, so that the dream of the real purpose of the establishment of the dear homeland — for which hundreds of thousands of people gave unparalleled sacrifices — may be fulfilled.

a. Promotion of the spirit of continuous action

b. Self-sufficiency in food

c. Educational progress

d. Establishment of social equality

e. Just distribution of resources

f. World peace and love

a. Promotion of the spirit of continuous action

There is a saying that he whose today is not better than his past yesterday has been ruined. (Maqalat-e-Hariri)

After the establishment of Pakistan, to make it prosperous and powerful it is necessary that continuous hard work be done. For the construction and progress of Pakistan, one's abilities should be spent through positive and constructive activities. All the Pakistani celebrities keep urging the promotion of this very spirit. The essence of the philosophy of the thinker of Pakistan Allama Muhammad Iqbal (may Allah have mercy on him) is this very thing, that Muslims should keep moving forward with courage, and this very is the message of the above address of the Quaid-e-Azam (may Allah have mercy on him). This very is that spirit which will make Pakistan an Islamic welfare realm in the real sense. The Pakistani public appears to be actuated by this very spirit.

b. Self-sufficiency in food

Food is the most basic need of man; therefore without self-sufficiency in it, progress and prosperity of any kind cannot even be imagined. The people of the country to whom food itself is not available will never take interest in national affairs. So far Pakistan is counted among the developing countries, but nature has enriched us with its blessings. The correct use of natural resources is the very method of ending poverty from Pakistan. The Quaid-e-Azam (may Allah have mercy on him) used to remain worried about this matter, that in our villages poverty is very great.

The government is making serious efforts for the ending of poverty. To a considerable extent self-sufficiency in food too has been attained. That time is not far when poverty will end from the dear homeland and all national resources will be put to best use.
